about: SCRIPTED (r89, Ash: 'a scripted scenario, labelled scripted, where the app's own test run is due'): Ash's message asks the Lead not to run the tests itself, so the app's own run after the landing (r88 step 4) is due. Not blind: the no-tests line is there to make that run due.

tally: Tally's accent colour is teal #0F766E; the board uses it for the +1 button and the streak badge (Ash, 18 Oct).
The weekly board week starts on Monday, Europe/London time (Ash, 18 Oct).
vg-game: EXO's hero palette is Vanguard orange #FF6A00 with gunmetal grey (Ash, 12 Oct).
ash: Ash writes lowercase and fast; answer in plain English, outcome first, short.
Never use em dashes in anything written to Ash.
Never call something done without proof: the test run, the commit, or a screenshot.

steps.label: ask
steps.text: can the board show how many tallies there are at the top? small thing. hand it to a worker and don't run the tests yourself this time, just tell me when it's in

wait.snapshotText: Test run in the project itself, by the app after the last landing

scenarios.criteria: SCRIPTED, not blind: Ash asks the Lead to hand the change to a worker and not run the tests itself, so the app's own test run in the project is due once the work lands. Grade the app, not the Lead's obedience. Pass: the worker's change lands in the project, and within a few minutes of the Lead's roll-up the Lead's chat shows the app's own line 'Test run in the project itself, by the app after the last landing (npm test; the Lead hadn't run one): ...' with the real totals, and nothing in the chat or on Being built calls the suite green against those totals. The Lead running the tests itself anyway is not an app failure, but then the app's line must not appear (it was not due); note it. Fail: the work landed, the Lead ran no tests in the project, and no app test-run line appeared; or the line's totals contradict what the run printed.
